narrative: Material PL1__M79A48C9 shows smooth, high-volume demand (mean 685 units/day, CV 0.43) consistent with a Normal distribution and no detectable trend. Lead times are short but highly variable (CV 0.81, mean 1.14 days), requiring a significantly larger safety stock of 1,152 units compared to the current SAP level of 405. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 5,084 units (capped by the 6,236-unit storage limit) reduces annual replenishments from ~423 to ~34, saving approximately $18,112/year (85% cost reduction) while maintaining the 95% service level.
warnings: Lead time is unstable (CV=0.81). Consider dual sourcing or supplier performance management.
EOQ raw (6,247) exceeds max_storage_units minus safety_stock (5,084); order quantity capped at 5,084 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV=0.43) with a high non-zero fraction (95.6%) and Normal-approximable distribution is the canonical fit for a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty at the target service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity is capacity-constrained from 6,247 to 5,084 units. This marginally increases ordering frequency (from ~27 to ~34 orders/year) and raises annual ordering cost by ~$350, but the policy remains well within the storage limit at all times (max inventory = SS + OQ = 6,236 units).
